angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 380,548 km at 29.40 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 34.0172 +/- 0.0255 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 29.40 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.547 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Awiphan et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 3470 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.463.2574A/abstract): 380,548 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.539 +/- 0.047 solar masses from Awiphan et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 3470 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.463.2574A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3600 +/- 100 K from Awiphan et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 3470 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.463.2574A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Awiphan et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 3470 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.463.2574A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-3470.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.694, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3470 (pscomppars): spectral type M1.5, from Kosiarek et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...97K/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3470 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.2 dex, from Awiphan et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.463.2574A/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3470 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.5376, from Kosiarek et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...97K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3470 (pscomppars): age 1.65 Gyr, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 3470 (pscomppars): rotation period 21.54 d, from Kosiarek et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...97K/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, LP 424-4: projected rotation speed 0.92 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2023A&A...676A..90R)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.547 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.716. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
